newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CREDIT LYONNAIS BELGIUM SEES RISE IN 1996 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: CREDIT LYONNAIS BELGIUM SEES RISE IN 1996 PROFIT.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium, a unit of French Credit Lyonnais, said on Tuesday it expected 1996 net profit of at least 800 million Belgian francs from 630 million in 1995.
"We foresee profit of at least 800 million and 1997 results will also rise," CLB chief executive officer Philippe Cloes told a news conference.
CLB also said in a statement that total savings deposits with CLB rose 11 percent to 102 billion francs in 1996, bringing it above the 100 billion level for the first time since 1994.
The bank also manages about 111 billion francs worth of investments for its clients.
CLB has 30 branches, 220,000 customers and employs 1,000 people.
Full year results are due to be released in the spring.
